mainTopic: Why blood is excluded from מעילה, נותר and טומאה; the rule that a finished מצוה has no מעילה and its exceptions
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the פסוק calls נותר and טומאה two kinds of 'profaning,' so they work alike. Then the גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's words 'except for the blood.' First it brings three teachings from ויקרא 17:11 that blood has no מעילה: עולא ('to you'), דבי רבי ישמעאל ('to atone'), and רבי יוחנן ('it is,' so blood before כפרה is like blood after כפרה). The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן with the rule that once a מצוה is done, there is no מעילה. It then deals with the exceptions to that rule: תרומת הדשן, the יום הכפורים garments, and the עגלה ערופה. These are two cases that come as one, and each also has a limiting word in its פסוק, so they teach nothing for other cases. Finally, the גמרא explains that the three words about blood exclude it from מעילה, נותר and טומאה. פיגול needs no פסוק, because blood is itself the מתיר. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן asks why the תורה mentions כרת three times for eating שלמים while impure.

steps.title: The verse speaks of two kinds of profaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier derivation: the פסוק is talking about two different 'profanings,' one from נותר and one from טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is talking about two kinds of profaning: one is the problem of נותר (leftover sacrificial meat), and the other is the problem of טומאה (ritual impurity).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a discussion from before this section by saying the פסוק covers two separate 'profanings': נותר and טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק groups נותר and טומאה together as two kinds of חילול, they are treated alike. Just as טומאה applies even to an item that has no מתיר (the thing that makes it permitted), נותר applies to such an item too.

keyTerms.meaning: Profaning; making something holy into something treated as ordinary
Sacrificial meat left past its allowed time to be eaten
Ritual impurity
A disqualification

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of why the משנה gives the same liability for נותר and טומאה even on items that have no פיגול liability.

phrases.english: The verse is speaking of two profanations;
phrases.notes: Since the two 'profanings' are listed together, נותר follows the same rule as טומאה here.

phrases.english: one is the disqualification of notar,
and one is the disqualification of ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a derivation that began before this section
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נותר and טומאה are both called 'profaning' by the פסוק, so נותר works like טומאה, even for an item that has no מתיר.

steps.title: Where do we learn that blood is excluded?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'except for the blood' and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Except for the blood.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's exception for blood and asks for its source. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said there is liability for נותר and טומאה on many items, but not on blood. The גמרא wants a פסוק that sets blood apart. Before answering this directly, it first brings teachings about blood and מעילה; the full answer comes in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for the blood (the משנה's words)
From where are these matters learned? A request for a source
'Etc.' The rest of the משנה's line is assumed

steps.confusionAlert: The three teachings that come next are about מעילה, not directly about נותר and טומאה. The גמרא uses them to set up its answer, so don't expect them to mention נותר.

phrases.english: Except for the blood, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: there is no liability for נותר or טומאה with blood.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה's exception for blood
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for excluding blood from the liabilities of נותר and טומאה

steps.title: עולא: 'I have given it to you' means blood is yours
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns from 'I have given it to you' that the blood belongs to you, so it is not הקדש property and has no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The פסוק says, 'And I have given it to you,' which means it shall be yours.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings a פסוק showing that blood is not subject to מעילה, because the Torah calls it 'yours.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה is the sin of using הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit. If the Torah says the blood is given 'to you,' it is not counted as Temple property, so there is no מעילה with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing הקדש property for personal benefit
It shall be yours

phrases.english: Ulla says: The verse states:
"And I have given it to you"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:11. The 'it' here is the blood.

phrases.english: it shall be yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a teaching about blood and מעילה to prepare the answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a קרבן is not subject to מעילה, because the Torah says 'to you,' meaning it is yours.

steps.title: דבי רבי ישמעאל: Blood is given for atonement, not for מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from 'to make atonement' that blood was given for כפרה and not to be subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The פסוק says 'to make atonement,' meaning: I gave it for atonement, and not for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second source is given for the same rule, taken from a different word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the focus is on the word 'לכפר.' The blood has one purpose, כפרה, so the rules of מעילה do not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught (a ברייתא)
To make atonement
Atonement

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא, אָמַר קְרָא:
phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: The verse states:
"To make atonement"
I gave it for atonement, and not for misuse of consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל תָּנָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different word in the same פסוק as the source for the same rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood is given for כפרה, not to be subject to מעילה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Blood before atonement is like blood after atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the word 'הוא' that blood before כפרה has the same status as after כפרה. Since there is no מעילה after כפרה, there is none before it either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The פסוק says 'it is,' teaching that before atonement it is the same as after atonement. Just as after atonement there is no מעילה, so too before atonement there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third source, from the word 'הוא,' comparing blood before its use to blood after its use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that once the מצוה has been done with a holy item, it no longer has מעילה. After the blood is put on the מזבח, its מצוה is done, so it has no מעילה. The word 'הוא' says the blood stays the same, so even before it is put on the מזבח it has no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is.' Read as 'it stays the same'
Before atonement, before the blood is put on the מזבח
After atonement, once the blood's מצוה is done
'Just as ... so too.' A comparison formula

steps.whatToRemember: Three sources teach that the blood of a קרבן has no מעילה: עולא ('to you,' it is yours), דבי רבי ישמעאל ('to atone,' not for מעילה), and רבי יוחנן ('it is,' before כפרה is like after כפרה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The verse states:
"It is"
phrases.notes: From the end of the same פסוק: 'for it is the blood that atones.'

phrases.english: it is before atonement as it is after atonement;

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַחַר כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: just as after atonement it is not subject to misuse of consecrated property,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה.
phrases.english: so too before atonement it is not subject to misuse of consecrated property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third source for the same rule, from a different word in the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood has no מעילה even before כפרה, because 'הוא' makes its status before כפרה match its status after כפרה.

steps.title: Why not compare the other way around?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: maybe 'הוא' means the blood after כפרה is like before כפרה, so it would have מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that after כפרה is like before כפרה: just as before כפרה there is מעילה on the blood, so too after כפרה there is מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's reading of the word 'הוא'. It flips the comparison in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said 'הוא' makes before and after כפרה the same, so there is no מעילה at any point. But a comparison can work in either direction. Why not say both stages have מעילה instead?

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead / maybe you could say
Atonement, done here by putting the blood on the מזבח
The prohibition of using הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit

phrases.english: Say instead: after atonement is like before atonement –
phrases.notes: The גמרא is flipping רבי יוחנן's comparison from step 5 in the other direction.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִפְנֵי כַּפָּרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: just as before atonement there is misuse of sacred property on it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה יֵשׁ בּוֹ מְעִילָה!
phrases.english: so too after atonement there is misuse of sacred property on it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the direction of רבי יוחנן's comparison in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading that 'הוא' makes before-כפרה like after-כפרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison can go either way, so the פסוק could just as well mean there is מעילה both before and after כפרה.

steps.title: Once the מצוה is done, there is no מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a general rule: nothing whose מצוה has been completed is still subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is nothing whose מצוה has already been done and that still has מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a known rule. After the blood is used for כפרה, its מצוה is done, so it cannot have מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison can only go one way. 'After כפרה' cannot have מעילה, because once a מצוה is done there is no מעילה. So 'before כפרה' must be compared to 'after', and there is no מעילה at either stage.

keyTerms.meaning: Its מצוה has been done
One commits מעילה with it

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule: once something's מצוה is finished, there is no more מעילה on it.

phrases.english: You have nothing whose מצוה has been done
and one still commits misuse with it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Invokes a general rule that fixes which way the comparison goes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison could go either way, so the blood might have מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: After כפרה there can be no מעילה, so the comparison must be 'before is like after': no מעילה at all.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁנַּעֲשֵׂית מִצְוָתוֹ וּמוֹעֲלִין בּוֹ

steps.title: What about תרומת הדשן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule: תרומת הדשן has its מצוה done and still has מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there really no such thing? But there is תרומת הדשן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 7 by pointing to a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תרומת הדשן, the ashes are removed from the מזבח, so their מצוה is done. Yet they must be buried and still have מעילה. That looks like a clear exception to the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so?! (a challenge)
But look at / but there is
Removing some of the ashes from the מזבח each morning

phrases.english: And is there not? But there is the removal of the ashes!
phrases.notes: Even after they are taken off the מזבח, these ashes still have מעילה. So here is a finished מצוה that still has מעילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule given as the answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that nothing whose מצוה is done has מעילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומת הדשן is a counterexample: its מצוה is done and it still has מעילה.

steps.title: Two verses that come as one do not teach
steps.stepSummary: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה both have this unusual law. Two such sources are treated as special exceptions and teach nothing for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its rule. תרומת הדשן is an exception, and an exception does not cancel the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two cases have the same unusual law: תרומת הדשן and the כהן גדול's בגדי כהונה. Each has מעילה even after its מצוה is done. When the תורה has to state the same special law twice, it shows the law is unusual. So we do not apply it anywhere else, and the general rule still stands for the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן's garments; here, the כהן גדול's white garments of יום כיפור
Two verses that teach the same special law
They do not teach (for other cases)

steps.confusionAlert: You might think two sources make a stronger proof than one. Here it is the reverse: the תורה stating the same special law twice shows that it is a special exception, not a general rule.

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes
and the priestly vestments
phrases.notes: These are the white garments the כהן גדול wears on יום כיפור. They also keep מעילה after use.

phrases.english: are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the counterexample: it is a special exception that cannot be applied elsewhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תרומת הדשן shows that a finished מצוה can still have מעילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two sources with the same special law, so they teach nothing for other cases. The general rule holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of learning from פסוקים: when two sources share one special law, that law is not applied to other cases.

steps.title: This works for the רבנן, who say the garments must be buried
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the answer works for the רבנן, who say the garments need גניזה. It is setting up a challenge from a different opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the רבנן, who say that 'and he shall leave them there' teaches that the garments must be put away (buried).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next challenge. It says the 'two verses' answer works for the רבנן, which hints that it may not work for someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learn from 'וְהִנִּיחָם שָׁם' that the כהן גדול's white garments must be buried, so they cannot be used again. That gives the garments their special law, so there really are two sources. The phrase 'הניחא' tells us an opinion that disagrees is about to be raised.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion; sets up a 'but for the other opinion' challenge)
'And he shall leave them there'
Putting away / burying something holy so it is not used

phrases.english: This works out well for the Rabbis, who say
"and he shall leave them there" –
teaches that they require burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts testing whether the answer of step 9 works for every opinion about בגדי כהונה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 9 that בגדי כהונה is a second source with the same special law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer depends on the רבנן's reading that the garments need גניזה. An opinion that disagrees would leave only one source. Step 11 completes this challenge with the view of רבי דוסא.

steps.title: According to רבי דוסא, the garments are no longer a second example
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the answer works for רבי דוסא, who lets an ordinary כהן use the garments. If so, תרומת הדשן is the only exception, and a single exception should teach for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי דוסא, who says the garments are allowed for an ordinary כהן, as long as the כהן גדול does not use them on another יום הכפורים, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it set up in the last step. It now asks how the answer works for רבי דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 9 needed two exceptions: תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה. רבי דוסא says the garments may be used by an ordinary כהן, so they are not an example of a lasting holiness that forbids use. That leaves תרומת הדשן alone, and one exception should become a model for other cases, including the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
What is there to say? A formula that presses a challenge

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Dosa,
who says: they are permitted to an ordinary priest,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the linen garments the כהן גדול wore on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: provided that he does not use them
on another Yom Kippur –
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא, דְּאָמַר: מוּתָּרוֹת הֵן לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 10 by bringing the opinion of רבי דוסא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 9, that תרומת הדשן and בגדי כהונה are two cases that come as one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי דוסא the garments may still be used, so only תרומת הדשן is left. A single case should serve as a model for others.

steps.title: The second example is the עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replaces the garments with עגלה ערופה. Together with תרומת הדשן, it makes two verses that come as one, which teach nothing for other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are two verses that come as one, and any two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי דוסא by finding a different second case: the עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה stays forbidden to use even after its מצוה is done, just like תרומת הדשן. So there are still two exceptions. Two exceptions are treated as special cases and are not copied to other cases, so the blood is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered person is found and the killer is unknown
Two verses that teach the same unusual law
They do not teach; the law is not extended to other cases

phrases.english: Because the removal of the ashes
and the heifer whose neck is broken
are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי תְּרוּמַת הַדֶּשֶׁן וְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה שְׁנֵי כְּתוּבִין הַבָּאִין כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי דוסא by bringing a different second case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Substitutes a different second example so there are still two exceptions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With the garments removed, תרומת הדשן stands alone and should teach for other cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: עגלה ערופה is the second case, so the rule still does not spread.

steps.title: What about the view that two such verses do teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the answer only works for the view that two verses that come as one teach nothing. It asks what the other view would say.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says they do not teach, but according to the one who says they do teach, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer, because it depends on one side of a known argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about two verses that come as one. Some say they teach nothing for other cases, and some say they do. For the second view, the pair תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה should make the rule spread to other cases, and the original problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
They do teach; the law is extended to other cases

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
they do not teach,
but according to the one who says they do teach
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 12 by showing it only works for one side of a מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 12, which relies on the rule that two verses that come as one do not teach.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that such pairs do teach, the pair should make the rule spread to other cases.

steps.title: Each verse has a word that limits the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that each פסוק has a limiting word: 'הערופה' for the עגלה ערופה and 'ושמו' for תרומת הדשן. These words keep the rule inside those two cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two limiting words are written. Here it says 'הערופה,' and there it says 'ושמו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even those who say two such verses teach would agree here, because the תורה limits each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הערופה' (the one whose neck was broken) points only to that calf. The word 'ושמו' ('and he shall put it') points only to those ashes. Since the תורה limits both cases, nothing can be learned from them, so the rule 'once the מצוה is done there is no מעילה' still stands for the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Limiting words that keep a law from spreading
'Whose neck was broken,' said about the עגלה ערופה
'And he shall put it,' said about תרומת הדשן

steps.whatToRemember: There is no מעילה once a מצוה is finished. תרומת הדשן and עגלה ערופה are exceptions, and the תורה uses a limiting word for each one, so they teach nothing for other cases.

phrases.english: Two exclusions are written;
here it is written: "whose neck was broken",
phrases.notes: דברים 21:6. This is about the עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: and there it is written: "and he shall put it".
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3. This is about תרומת הדשן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by showing the פסוקים themselves limit each case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in each פסוק restricts the law to that case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the view that two verses that come as one do teach, the rule should spread to other cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each פסוק limits its own case, so even that view agrees nothing is learned from them.

steps.title: Why do we need three verses about blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why three separate verse-words are needed to exclude blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need three verses about blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. Earlier, three teachers each learned from the same פסוק that blood is not subject to מעילה. Why do we need all three?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, עולא ('לכם'), the school of רבי ישמעאל ('לכפר'), and רבי יוחנן ('הוא') each pointed to a different word in ויקרא 17:11 to exclude blood. One exclusion should be enough. So each extra word must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Three verses (here, three exclusion-words in the פסוק)
Why do I need it?
Blood of a קרבן

phrases.english: And why do I need three verses about blood?
phrases.notes: These are the three words learned earlier from ויקרא 17:11, each one used to exclude blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the three exclusion-words about blood that were learned earlier on the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three extra exclusion-words for blood is teaching.

steps.title: Each verse removes blood from a different law
steps.stepSummary: One word excludes blood from מעילה, one from נותר, and one from טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: To exclude blood from מעילה, from נותר, and from טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the three words are not extra. Each one takes blood out of a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One word teaches that using the blood is not מעילה. One teaches that leftover blood is not נותר. One teaches that eating it while impure is not the sin of eating holy food while impure. Someone who eats the blood is still punished, but only for eating blood.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out of a rule
Misusing הקדש property
Meat of a קרבן left past its time
Eating holy food while impure

steps.confusionAlert: Blood is not becoming permitted. Eating it is still the sin of eating blood. The words only teach that the extra sins of נותר and טומאה do not apply to it.

phrases.english: To exclude it from מעילה,
from נותר, and from טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15, and in doing so gives the source the משנה's 'except for the blood' needed, which step 2 asked for.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each extra verse-word its own job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three words for one exclusion look like too many.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each word removes blood from a separate law: מעילה, נותר, and טומאה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three words exclude blood from מעילה, נותר, and טומאה.

steps.title: No verse is needed to exclude blood from פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A משנה already teaches that the thing that makes an offering permitted is not subject to פיגול, and blood is that thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But פיגול does not need a verse, as we learned: anything that has permitting items, whether for people or for the altar, makes one liable for פיגול. And the blood itself is the permitting item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא heads off a question: why is there no fourth word to exclude blood from פיגול? It answers that a משנה already teaches this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says פיגול applies to things that have something else making them permitted. The permitting item itself is not covered. Blood is the permitting item, since sprinkling it permits the meat to people and the fats to the מזבח. So blood is automatically outside פיגול, and no פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made unfit by a wrong intention about time; eating it brings כרת
The items that make an offering permitted
Itself

steps.whatToRemember: Blood has three exclusion-words, for מעילה, נותר and טומאה. פיגול needs no word, because blood is the מתיר, and a מתיר is not subject to פיגול.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key rule of פיגול: it applies to what is permitted by the blood, not to the blood that does the permitting.

phrases.english: But פיגול does not need a verse,
as we learned: anything that has permitting items,
whether for a person or for the altar,
one is liable for it because of פיגול.
And blood itself is the permitting item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 16 by explaining why פיגול is missing from the list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a gap in the list by pointing to an existing source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since blood is excluded from three similar laws, a fourth word should be needed for פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's rule that only things with מתירין are subject to פיגול already leaves out blood, which is itself the מתיר.
steps.raayaObject: Blood is not subject to פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on 43a: כל שיש לו מתירין

steps.title: Why does the תורה say כרת three times about impure שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks why the תורה mentions כרת three times for eating שלמים while impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why are there three mentions of כרת about שלמים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רבי יוחנן asks a question, and this sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment of כרת for eating שלמים while impure appears in three פסוקים: ויקרא 7:20, 7:21, and 22:3. One mention should be enough. The question assumes each extra mention must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Mentions of the punishment of כרת
Peace offerings
Why?

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
Why are there three mentions of כרת about שלמים?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20, 7:21, and 22:3, all about eating holy food while impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שְׁלֹשָׁה כָּרֵיתוֹת בִּשְׁלָמִים לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of blood ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three mentions of כרת for eating שלמים while impure comes to teach.
